post.title: Money dysmorphia: 64% of millionaires didn't feel wealthy
post.ig:
In 2025, 64% of US millionaires didn't call themselves wealthy.

Northwestern Mutual's 2025 study (Harris Poll, 4,626 US adults, Jan 2025): only 36% of people with $1M+ in investable assets called themselves wealthy.
Credit Karma's survey of 1,006 US adults (Dec 2023): 29% report "money dysmorphia", 43% of Gen Z and 41% of millennials. It's a popular term, not a clinical diagnosis.
Schwab Modern Wealth Survey 2025: $839,000 to feel comfortable vs $2.3 million to be wealthy, a $1.46M gap.
Fed SHED (nearly 13,000 adults, Oct 2025): 73% doing at least okay financially.

Sources: Northwestern Mutual Planning & Progress Study 2025, Charles Schwab Modern Wealth Survey 2025, Intuit Credit Karma/Qualtrics, Federal Reserve SHED report (May 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
